qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Gas turbine installed base under long-term service agreements and proprietary high-voltage grid transmission technology provide sticky switching barriers; however, the business has been severely burdened by quality defect liabilities in Siemens Gamesa wind turbines, fixed-price project exposure, and government guarantee dependencies.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). Long-cycle wind turbine and heavy energy equipment purchase trap. Severe quality defects and component failures in Siemens Gamesa onshore wind turbines resulted in multi-billion-euro warranty provisions, an operational collapse in FY2023 (-EUR 4.5B net loss), and reliance on a EUR 15B German federal government rescue guarantee package. Structural execution risks and long-cycle fixed-price project liabilities cap the competitive advantage period far below the 15-year hurdle.
qualitative.evidence: Operating history reflects extreme cyclicality and execution volatility: FY2022 EBIT of -EUR 456M and NI of -EUR 467M; FY2023 EBIT of -EUR 3,098M and NI of -EUR 4,532M driven by massive Siemens Gamesa quality defects and warranty provisions. While FY2024 and FY2025 staged a strong recovery (FY25 EBIT EUR 2,506M, NI EUR 1,414M) driven by booming Grid Technologies and Gas Services, the business required a EUR 15B state-backed guarantee backstop in late 2023. Long-cycle fixed-price contract risks, heavy warranty liabilities, and intense global turbine competition cap CAP at 5 years.
